tasks.short: Check loading and fuel against weight and balance limits

steps.what: Collect and reconcile passenger, cargo distributions and fuel inputs
Transfer checked inputs into the flight mass and balance application
Check weight and balance specifications and accept the final load sheet

tasks.design: Configure the existing {OTHER} flight mass and balance application to import checked loading inputs. Retain reconciliation and final pilot acceptance; existing calculation runtime earns no saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate loading and fuel reports can require repeated entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing mass and balance software can support mobile load sheets.
tasks.still_hard: An apparently valid mass category can describe the wrong passengers.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge implausible loading and refuse an unsafe departure.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated entry where an approved interface exists; flight authority is unchanged.

reach.learn: Load categories and aircraft configuration control

evidence.claim: NetLine/Load CockpitMobile supports pilot weight and balance calculations and mobile load sheet approval.
The proposed reduction concerns repeated input entry, with no measured pilot labour saving established.

assumptions: Boundary is pilot checking, input entry and acceptance, excluding physical loading and fuel delivery.

Load controller produces flight id, aircraft configuration version, passenger categories and counts, compartment masses and loading revision; fueler produces fuel quantity, units and timestamp during existing loading work. Their capture is retained without saving and requires no additional interface-only fields.
Pilot reconciliation and missing-field capture remain in s1 at 35 hours; transfer verification remains 15 hours in s2. Unsupported fields or stale revisions require full manual entry and checking.
Test native import configuration first; no new calculation engine or model inference.
Only repeated entry changes. Final loading approval binds the current inputs and calculation version.
unknowns: Whether pilots currently re-enter these inputs
Available approved interface and aircraft configurations
research_questions: Does timed comparison show less input entry while preserving reconciliation and acceptance?

incremental.description: Review interface exceptions and configuration changes
Maintain approved field mapping and regression checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact flight, aircraft configuration, loading revision, fuel timestamp and calculated load sheet; any change voids acceptance

tasks.human_edge: Ask follow-up questions and establish a common understanding.

tasks.short: Order safety changes to the flight plan or load

steps.what: Assess safety implications of fuel supplies, loads, routes and schedules
Order changes and confirm understanding with the responsible operating teams

tasks.design: Retain pilot assessment in {OTHER} flight planning and direct change instructions through {TELEPHONY}. Existing recalculation tools support the decision without replacing it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes affect interacting safety margins and operating teams.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital planning tools already recalculate route and fuel alternatives.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing an acceptable action with incomplete and changing information.
tasks.human_edge: Take responsibility for safety changes and check their understanding.
tasks.altitude: Decision rights and coordination time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Lido Flight 4D supports route and fuel planning against weather and airspace restrictions.

assumptions: Boundary ends at confirmed instructions; physical changes and dispatcher execution retain their own labour.

Zero upkeep because the process is unchanged.
